headline: Chargeback Fees by Processor (2026 Guide)
description: How chargebacks and disputes affect Stripe, PayPal, and Square sellers—why dollar fees vary, how to budget reserves, and where to verify official dispute costs.

mainEntity.name: How much is a Stripe chargeback fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: It varies and changes—check Stripe’s official dispute documentation for your country and product. Do not rely on memorized dollar amounts from old articles. Budget a reserve based on your own history plus Stripe’s current published fee.

PayPal’s dispute and chargeback-related costs vary by product and outcome. Confirm on PayPal’s official help and fee pages. Processing for US G&S is 2.99% (no fixed) as of 2026-10-24; Checkout is 3.49% + $0.49, separate from dispute fees.

Square likewise publishes dispute-related fees that can change. Verify on Square’s official support/pricing materials. Card-present vs online activity can show different dispute patterns even when online processing lists 2.9% + $0.30.

mainEntity.name: Should dispute fees decide my processor?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are one factor beside processing rates, conversion, payout timing, and category fit. Model processing with our calculators, then add your measured dispute loss rate—not a generic internet rumor.

mainEntity.name: How do I price after both fees and chargebacks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reverse-calculate processing fees for your target net, then increase prices to cover your historical dispute/refund loss rate. See how to price after fees for the processing algebra.
